place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 外门 · 饭堂门口
place.en: Chending Temple · The outer court · the refectory door

setup.zh: 九月初十，天没亮，饭堂门口排起了长龙：周衡发腰牌、灵石，马小宝收公中。身后有人拍你肩膀——阿禾。
setup.en: The tenth of the ninth month, before dawn, a long queue at the refectory door: Zhou Heng hands out waist tags and spirit stones, Ma Xiaobao collects the common fund. Someone taps your shoulder from behind — Ahe.

recap.zh: 入门第二天，阿禾下山来找你——昨天测出木天灵根，观主收了亲传；外门的灰袍底下露着一线青，「青的扎眼」。她在小本子上记了你一笔：杂灵根——「哪天你不是了，好对账」。
recap.en: Your second day in the sect, Ahe came down the mountain to find you — yesterday she tested as a heavenly wood root and the Abbot took her as his own disciple; a thread of green showed under her outer-sect grey robe ("green stands out"). She wrote you into her little notebook: mixed root — "so we can check the books the day you're not."

zh: 九月初十，饭堂门口，领灵石，交公中。
身后有人拍你的肩膀——一个红鼻头。
en: The tenth of the ninth month, the refectory door: draw stones, pay the common fund.
Someone taps your shoulder — a red nose.
"The day you're not, we check the books."

story.zh:
沉鼎山外门的日子，沈小满是从交钱开始过的——钱还没捂热，便有人伸手来收。九月初十，天还没亮透。外门几十间灰瓦房顺着东坡一层一层叠上去，瓦楞上浮着一层白气——不是炊烟，是山里的灵气夜里沉下来，叫早上的风一赶，贴着屋脊慢慢地流。饭堂门口已排起了长龙。一百来个新弟子，穿着昨夜才领的灰袍，袍子是照着大个子裁的，小个子穿上，下摆拖到脚面，远远看过去，像一群刚出窝的灰鸭子。

饭堂门口摆一张榆木桌子，桌子后面坐着外门执事周衡。周衡是个三十来岁的瘦高个儿，一脸愁苦，面前摊着一本厚得能当枕头使的账簿，叫一个名字，发一块枣木腰牌，三块灵石。那灵石有鸽子蛋大小，石皮发灰，里头却隐隐透出一点光来，像雪地里埋着的一粒火星。周衡发一个人，便抬头看那人一眼，道一声：「有前途！」发到第三十几个，那三个字已经说得像念经。轮到小满，他看了看名册上「五行杂灵根」那几个字，端详了小满好一会儿，道：「……有前途。」没有那个叹号。

进了饭堂的门，往前走不上十步，又是一张桌子。桌子后面坐着马小宝，面前摆一只描金的小木匣，匣上贴一张红纸，写着两个大字：**公中**。他身后站着两个进门三年的老弟子，抱着胳膊，像庙门口的两尊泥塑。唱名的那个执事——码头上冲白衣人点头、正殿里替马小宝添了一道的那一个——是马三的表哥，马小宝的表伯；一夜之间，马小宝便成了「马师兄」。周衡瞧了那匣子一眼，低头接着发——名册在唱名执事手里。排在小满前头的孙二狗，背上还背着那个比他身子还大的包袱，捧着三块灵石看了半天，拣出最小的一块，哆哆嗦嗦地放进了匣子。他刚要走，身后那尊泥塑伸出一条腿来，在他脚后跟上一勾，他背着那个大包袱往前一栽，脚下踉跄了三四步，歪歪斜斜，像一根给风吹弯了的芦苇，弯到了地皮上，偏偏又弹了回来——竟没有倒。

小满拣了一块不大不小的，放进匣子里。马小宝眯起眼睛：「就这么交了？」小满道：「规矩嘛。小宝哥辛苦。」马小宝道：「叫马师兄。」小满道：「马师兄辛苦。」马小宝满意地一扬下巴，腰上一块旧木牌晃了一晃，一面刻着「巡夜」两个字——外门没人肯接的差事，他表伯偏偏派给了他。小满凑得近，鼻子里忽然钻进一股味儿：不是桂花糕的甜，是一股青苦的草腥气，凉丝丝的，吸进去，肚子底下那口枯井，竟像给凉水激了一下。马小宝一夜巡回来，身上带的就是这个。

身后忽然有人拍他肩膀。

小满回头一看，是一个扎两根小辫子的姑娘，灰袍比他的还大一号，袖子挽了三道，下摆拿草绳在腰里扎了一圈；领口底下，露出一线青。一个红鼻头，冻得像一根萝卜。手里捏着一个巴掌大的小本子，一截炭条夹在耳朵上。

小满道：「……阿禾。你躲了我一整天。」

阿禾道：「嗯，是躲着你。」

「你怎么下来了？观主的院子在山顶上。」

「走下来的。」阿禾道，「石阶上，我从你边上冲过去的。洛书，我比你先摆好半炷香。」她顿了一顿，一本正经地道，「考试的时候，不认人。认了你，要分心。」小满道：「那现在呢？」阿禾道：「现在考完了。」

小满瞧了瞧她领口那一线青，又瞧了瞧她身上这件灰袍——外门的。「你这身……」阿禾把领口往上拽了一拽：「借的。青的扎眼。」她往饭堂里头瞟了一眼。唱名的那个执事坐在马小宝身后，端着茶碗，眼睛在新弟子脸上一张一张地过。

小满问：「你怎么没跟我一起来？」

阿禾道：「我娘说，你一个人去，会死。我一个人去，也会死。两个人一起去，死一双，不划算。所以分开走。」小满想了一想，觉得这话虽然难听，账倒是算得明白。阿禾舔了舔炭条，又记了一笔，道：「杂灵根。」
story.en:
Shen Xiaoman's days in the outer sect of Sunken Cauldron Mountain began with paying up: the money wasn't even warm in his hand before someone reached out to collect it. The tenth day of the ninth month, not yet properly light. The outer sect's few dozen grey-tiled houses were stacked up the east slope tier on tier, and over the ridges of their tiles floated a white haze. It wasn't kitchen smoke. It was the mountain's spirit qi, which sank at night and was driven by the morning wind to flow slowly along the roof ridges. A long line had already formed at the door of the dining hall. A hundred or so new disciples in the grey robes they had drawn only last night; the robes were cut to fit the big ones, so on the small ones the hems dragged over their feet, and from a distance they looked like a flock of grey ducklings just out of the nest.

At the door of the dining hall stood an elm table, and behind it sat the outer sect steward, Zhou Heng. Zhou Heng was a tall, thin man of thirty or so with a careworn face. Spread open in front of him was a ledger thick enough to use as a pillow. He called a name, handed out a jujube-wood waist token and three spirit stones. The spirit stones were the size of pigeon eggs, grey-skinned, but a faint light showed through from inside them, like a spark buried in snow. For each person he gave to, Zhou Heng looked up at them once and said, "Promising!" By somewhere past the thirtieth, the word was coming out like a sutra. When it was Xiaoman's turn, he looked at the words "five-element mixed spirit root" in the register, studied Xiaoman for a good while, and said, "...Promising." Without the exclamation mark.

Inside the dining hall door, not ten steps further on, was another table. Behind it sat Ma Xiaobao, with a small gilt-painted wooden box in front of him. On the box was pasted a sheet of red paper with two big characters: **Common Fund**. Behind him stood two disciples three years in, arms folded, like the two clay guardians at a temple gate. The name-calling steward (the one who had nodded to the man in white on the landing, who had added a stroke for Ma Xiaobao in the main hall) was Ma San's cousin, Ma Xiaobao's uncle; overnight, Ma Xiaobao had become "Senior Brother Ma". Zhou Heng glanced at the box and lowered his head to go on handing out. The register was in the name-calling steward's hands. Sun Ergou, ahead of Xiaoman in the line, still carrying the bundle bigger than he was on his back, held his three spirit stones and looked at them for a long time, then picked out the smallest and, shaking, put it in the box. He was just about to walk on when one of the clay guardians behind stuck out a leg and hooked his heel. Bundle and all, he pitched forward and stumbled three or four steps, lurching, like a reed bent by the wind, bent right down to the dirt, and then sprang back. He didn't fall.

Xiaoman picked one neither big nor small and put it in the box. Ma Xiaobao narrowed his eyes. "Just like that?" Xiaoman said, "It's the rule. Thanks for your trouble, Brother Xiaobao." Ma Xiaobao said, "Call me Senior Brother Ma." Xiaoman said, "Thanks for your trouble, Senior Brother Ma." Ma Xiaobao lifted his chin, satisfied, and an old wooden token at his waist swung. On one side were carved two characters: Night Watch. It was a job nobody in the outer sect would take, and his uncle had handed it to him of all people. Xiaoman was standing close, and a smell suddenly got into his nose: not the sweetness of osmanthus cake, but a green, bitter, grassy rankness, cool, and when he breathed it in, the dry well down in his belly started as if splashed with cold water. That was what Ma Xiaobao brought back on him after a night on watch.

Suddenly someone behind him tapped his shoulder.

Xiaoman turned and saw a girl with two little plaits. Her grey robe was a size bigger than his, the sleeves rolled up three times, the hem gathered with a straw rope at the waist; under her collar showed a line of green. A red nose, frozen like a radish. In her hand she held a little notebook the size of her palm, and a stick of charcoal was tucked behind her ear.

Xiaoman said, "...Ahe. You've been avoiding me a whole day."

Ahe said, "Mm. I was avoiding you."

"How did you get down here? The Abbot's courtyard is at the top of the mountain."

"I walked down," Ahe said. "On the steps, I was the one who rushed past you. The Luo Writing, I had it done half a stick of incense before you." She paused, and said very seriously, "In an exam you don't know anybody. Knowing you would've been a distraction." Xiaoman said, "And now?" Ahe said, "Now the exam's over."

Xiaoman looked at the line of green at her collar, then at the grey robe she had on: outer sect. "What you're wearing..." Ahe tugged her collar up. "Borrowed. Green stands out." She glanced into the dining hall. The name-calling steward sat behind Ma Xiaobao with a tea bowl, his eyes going over the new disciples' faces one by one.

Xiaoman asked, "Why didn't you come with me?"

Ahe said, "My ma said if you go on your own you'll die. If I go on my own I'll die too. If we go together, two die, and that's a bad deal. So we go separately." Xiaoman thought about it, and felt that though it wasn't nice to hear, the sums were clear enough. Ahe licked her charcoal, wrote something else down, and said, "Mixed spirit root."

exits.means: lets Ahe's entry stand and means to prove it wrong, goes on to the lesson

what.zh: 外门第一天，阿禾在小本子上记了你一笔：杂灵根。你说：哪天不是了，拿本子来对。
what.en: Your first day in the outer sect: Ahe wrote you into the little notebook — mixed root. You said: the day it isn't so, bring the notebook and check.

story.zh:
小满想了一想，道：「记吧。哪天我不是了，你拿本子来对。」

阿禾点了点头，像是他总算说了一句像样的话。她转身往山上走了。

小满站在原地，瞧着她那两截小辫子一跳一跳地走远了，心里头说不出是什么滋味。他想起出门那天，老槐树底下只站着他娘一个人。他那时候还道这丫头在睡懒觉。

原来她早走了一天，走的是另一条路。如今她走的，还是另一条路——往山顶上去。

那几天，小满逢人便问一句：太华山多远？孙二狗不知道。讲堂上一个老弟子听见了，笑他：「西边，两千来里，雍州。太华山上的太一宫。你问它做什么？」小满没说做什么。两千来里。他跟石蛋说的是，不远。
story.en:
Xiaoman thought it over and said, "Write it down. The day I'm not, bring the notebook and we'll check."

Ahe nodded, as if he had finally said something sensible. She turned and went off up the mountain.

Xiaoman stood where he was and watched her two little braids bob away, and could not have said what he felt. He remembered the day he left: under the old locust tree there had been only his mother. He had supposed the girl was sleeping in.

In fact she had left a day earlier, by another road. And the road she was on now was another road still: up to the top of the mountain.

Those few days, Xiaoman asked everyone he met the same thing: how far was Mount Taihua? Sun Ergou didn't know. An old disciple in the lecture hall heard him and laughed. "West. Two thousand li or so, in Yong Province. The Taiyi Palace on Mount Taihua. What do you want with it?" Xiaoman didn't say what. Two thousand li or so. What he had told Shidan was, not far.

exits.means: balks at being written down; she keeps it to check later

what.zh: 外门第一天，阿禾在小本子上记了你一笔：杂灵根。「哪天你不是了，好对账。」
what.en: Your first day in the outer sect: Ahe wrote you into the little notebook — mixed root. "So we can check the books the day you're not."

story.zh:
小满道：「这也记？」

阿禾道：「记着。哪天你不是了，好对账。」她转身往山上走了。

小满瞧着她那两截小辫子一跳一跳地走远了，心里头说不出是什么滋味。出门那天，老槐树底下只站着他娘一个人，他还道这丫头在睡懒觉。原来她早走了一天，走的是另一条路。如今她走的，还是另一条路——往山顶上去。

那几天，小满逢人便问一句：太华山多远？孙二狗不知道。讲堂上一个老弟子听见了，笑他：「西边，两千来里，雍州。太华山上的太一宫。你问它做什么？」小满没说做什么。两千来里。他跟石蛋说的是，不远。
story.en:
Xiaoman said, "You're writing that down too?"

Ahe said, "I'm keeping it. The day you're not one any more, we can check the accounts." She turned and went off up the mountain.

Xiaoman watched her two little plaits bob away into the distance and couldn't have said what he felt. On the day he left home, only his mother had been standing under the old locust tree, and he'd thought the girl was sleeping in. In fact she had left a day earlier, by another road. And the road she was on now was another road still: up to the top of the mountain.

Those few days, Xiaoman asked everyone he met the same thing: how far was Mount Taihua? Sun Ergou didn't know. An old disciple in the lecture hall heard him and laughed. "West. Two thousand li or so, in Yong Province. The Taiyi Palace on Mount Taihua. What do you want with it?" Xiaoman didn't say what. Two thousand li or so. What he had told Shidan was, not far.
